tagline: AI-first code editor built on VS Code

name: Claude
rankReason: Our pick for long documents, careful writing, and coding help, with a free plan to start.
tagline: Anthropic assistant for reasoning, writing, and code
description: Claude is Anthropic's AI assistant known for long-context analysis, careful writing, and strong coding help across chat and projects. On November 9, 2026, Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2, its most capable model for demanding technical work in coding, finance, and the sciences. Fable 5.2 has a 1M-token context window, generates output up to 30% faster than Fable 5.1, and costs less on the API at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens (down from $10 and $50). In the Claude apps it is available on the paid Pro, Max, Ultra, Team, and Enterprise plans from the model picker, and it is also in Claude Code and Cowork. On November 10, 2026, Anthropic added Claude Whiteboards (a shared board Claude turns into timelines and action items) and Claude Sheets (spreadsheets with tabs, formulas, and drop-downs that Claude builds and edits with you) in beta on all paid plans, made Claude Data generally available, and launched Claude Meetings in beta on Team and Enterprise plans, which adds Claude to Google Meet calls as a visible participant.
pricingNote: Free plan; Pro is $20 per month ($17 a month billed annually), Max is $100 per month, and the new Ultra plan is $200 per month; Team and Enterprise plans for organizations
strength: Long-context analysis, careful writing, and strong coding help, with Fable 5.2, Whiteboards, and Sheets on paid plans.
watchOut: Fable 5.2 and the newer Whiteboards, Sheets, Data, and Meetings features are on paid plans, not the free plan.
apiPricing: Fable 5.2 on the API costs $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens

name: ChatGPT
rankReason: OpenAI's general assistant for questions, writing, documents, images, and code, free to start.
tagline: OpenAI's flagship conversational AI
description: ChatGPT is OpenAI's general-purpose assistant for chat, writing, coding, image generation, and browsing. Broadest everyday AI starting point. As of November 4, 2026, Images 2.6 is available in ChatGPT, Codex, and the API, with GIF support and faster image edits. On November 13, 2026, OpenAI introduced ChatGPT Wallet, which lets agents pay on your behalf without getting your actual card details and asks for a security check, such as Face ID or a fingerprint, before every purchase. It begins rolling out in dots, so a dot can complete purchases for you, for ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and older in the US with eligible US-issued cards.
pricingNote: Free plan for everyone. Go is $8 a month, Plus is $20 a month, and Pro starts at $100 a month (higher Pro tiers are not shown). Business Standard is $20 per seat a month billed yearly or $25 billed monthly. Business Premium is $100 per seat a month billed yearly or $125 billed monthly.
strength: OpenAI's flagship conversational AI for everyday Q&A, drafting content, and quick coding help.
watchOut: Higher Pro tiers were not shown on the official pricing page.

name: Gemini
rankReason: Google's assistant for multimodal research, with Gmail help on Google AI Plus and Docs help on Google AI Pro. Free plan to start.
tagline: Google's multimodal AI across web and Workspace
description: Gemini is Google's AI assistant with deep Google ecosystem ties, multimodal understanding, and strong research workflows. On November 10, 2026, Google released Gemini 4 Carbon, its strongest model, built for long, multi-step work such as complex coding and debugging, dense document analysis, and scientific research; it uses more tokens than Gemini 4 Argon to reason and verify, while Argon remains Google's pick for most everyday work. Carbon is rolling out to Google AI Ultra subscribers in the Gemini app, AI Mode in Search, and Google Antigravity, and it is on the Gemini API paid tier at an introductory $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens until November 30, 2026, then $4 and $20. On November 11, 2026, Google also introduced the Gemini Decisions API, powered by its new Gemini Decision 1 model, which answers up to 1,000 yes or no, multiple-choice, and rubric-scoring questions about one text, image, audio, video, or PDF input in a single pass, at $0.10 per million input tokens with no output tokens billed. On November 12, 2026, Google released Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast model for everyday coding and agent work and its upgrade from Gemini 3.8 Flash. It is rolling out to everyone in the Gemini app model menu and in Google Search, free Gemini app users get it through automatic model selection, and the Gemini API price is $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens, flat across its 1 million token context window.
pricingNote: Free with a Google account; Google AI Plus is $4.99, Google AI Pro $19.99, and Google AI Ultra is $99.99 or $199.99 per month (US prices). Gmail help starts on Google AI Plus; Docs help needs Google AI Pro
strength: Multimodal assistant across the web and Google Workspace, including Drive content.
watchOut: Listed Google AI Plus, Pro, and Ultra prices are US rates; Ultra has $99.99 and $199.99 tiers. Gmail help starts on Google AI Plus, and Docs help needs Google AI Pro. Confirm local pricing.

The latest version, Nano Banana 2.1, was published by Google DeepMind on October 6, 2026. Google says it improves visual quality, text rendering, multi-turn character consistency, and mask-based editing, and it makes images at 1K, 2K, and 4K with search-grounded generation. It runs in the Gemini app, Google AI Mode in Search, Google Flow, Google AI Studio, and the Gemini API. Nano Banana 2 is the free option in the Gemini app, and Nano Banana Pro is the earlier Gemini 3 Pro Image model.

strength: Google's image model for conversational photo editing and accurate text, free in the Gemini app and cheap per image in the API.
watchOut: The newest version, Nano Banana 2.1, needs a paid Google AI plan in the Gemini app, the API has no free tier for image models, and Google does not publish the free plan's image limit. The original Nano Banana model was shut down Oct 2, 2026.

It can make animated GIFs and make backgrounds transparent, and the API adds markup-guided edits, SVG output, and a complexity setting. bestFor: repeated edits that keep details consistent

strength: Image creation and editing built into ChatGPT on every plan, with GIFs, markup edits, and fast Flare and detailed Sunburst API models.
watchOut: Free users get an image limit OpenAI does not publish, and API cost is per token, so the price per image depends on size, quality, and complexity.

strength: Artistic AI image generation well suited to concept art, stylized marketing visuals, and creative exploration.

Each teammate can use your Computer tasks, skills, memory, and tools, work with other teammates, and message coworkers in Slack. Computer can also run fully on-device on supported Apple-silicon Macs for Pro, Max, and Enterprise subscribers (Mac app 26.42.0 or later, 36 GB of unified memory recommended), so with your permission it can work across local files and Mac apps such as Notes and Mail without sending that personal data to the cloud.
bestFor: private local Computer tasks on a Mac

strength: AI search with cited answers, plus agent work with Teammates and private local Computer tasks on a Mac.

rankReason: Natural-sounding voiceovers, voice cloning, and dubbing in many languages. The free plan is for personal use only.
tagline: AI voice synthesis and cloning
description: ElevenLabs creates natural text-to-speech, voice clones, and dubbing for podcasts, products, and video. On November 10, 2026, ElevenLabs launched Scribe v3, its most accurate speech to text model for recorded audio, which it says makes 27% fewer word errors than Scribe v2 across 102 languages and has the lowest speaker-labeling error of the models it tested, plus Scribe v3 Live for real-time audio, which adds speaker labels to live transcription for the first time and improves turn detection for voice agents. Both are the default in the ElevenLabs app and are in the ElevenLabs API at $0.20 per hour for Scribe v3 and $0.22 per hour for Scribe v3 Live.
pricingNote: Free plan with 10,000 credits a month and no commercial license; Starter is $6 per month and adds a commercial license, Creator $22, and Pro $99; Scale and Business plans for teams; Scribe v3 speech to text API $0.20 per hour
strength: Realistic voiceovers, podcast narration, and multilingual dubbing, plus a Scribe speech-to-text API.
watchOut: The free plan has 10,000 credits a month and no commercial license; Starter is the first plan that adds one.

rankReason: Text-to-video, image-to-video, and video editing in one app, on credit plans from $12 a month.
tagline: AI video generation and editing
description: Runway offers generative video and image models plus editing tools for filmmakers, marketers, and creators producing short clips from text or images. Plans are credit-based across Gen-4.5 and partner models, with App Studio and Runway Ads on paid tiers.

strength: AI video generation and editing on credit-based Standard, Pro, and Max plans.
watchOut: The 125 free credits are one-time, not a monthly allowance, and extra credits start at a 1,000-credit minimum.

pricingNote: Included with Claude Pro ($20 a month, or $17 billed annually), Max ($100 a month), and Ultra ($200 a month); not included in the Free plan
strength: Anthropic's agentic coding in the terminal, using your Claude subscription or API.
watchOut: There is no standalone price in this listing; you need a Claude subscription or an Anthropic API key.

name: OpenAI Codex
rankReason: OpenAI's coding agent, included with every ChatGPT plan, Free included for quick tasks.
tagline: OpenAI's open-source coding agent for your terminal
description: OpenAI Codex is OpenAI's coding agent. The open-source Codex CLI reads your repo, edits files, and runs commands inside a sandbox with permission controls, and you can sign in with ChatGPT or use an API key. Version 0.167.0 (November 6, 2026) added an agent command center (codex agents) that marks unread results, switching between connected backends without losing your draft, local image previews while you compose, Google Cloud Vertex AI setup during sign-in, and expandable patch details inside approval prompts. GPT-6.1 Sol became its default model in version 0.161.0 on October 7.
bestFor: managing several agent sessions from one command center
pricingNote: Included in ChatGPT Free, Go, Plus, Pro (plans at $100, $200, or $500 a month), Business, Edu, and Enterprise plans, and shares usage limits with ChatGPT Work; API-key use is billed at API prices
strength: OpenAI's open-source coding agent that runs in your terminal.
watchOut: You sign in with a ChatGPT plan or an OpenAI API key; plan details are on the official Codex page.

name: Google Antigravity
rankReason: Google's free coding agent across an app, CLI, IDE extensions, and SDK, with weekly limits on the free plan.
tagline: Google's agentic coding platform across App, CLI, IDE, and SDK
description: Google Antigravity is an agentic coding platform for building with AI agents across an app, CLI, IDE, and SDK. Aimed at developers who want agent-driven workflows inside Google's AI stack. Since November 10, 2026, Google AI Ultra subscribers can use Gemini 4 Carbon, Google's strongest model, in Antigravity, and Google is previewing /swarm, which turns one prompt into a coordinated team of agents working in parallel isolated workspaces that you can track in real time. On November 12, 2026, Google added Gemini 4 Hydrogen for paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers and introduced Orchestrator, which switches between models such as Carbon and Hydrogen within one session; Google says Orchestrator reached near-Carbon task success on Terminal-Bench 4.0 while using 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster on average. On November 13, 2026, Google added Dynamic Workflows: type /run-workflow and the agent writes a short Python script that runs many agents in parallel or one after another, shows you the script to approve before it runs, and can save it for reuse. Dynamic Workflows are available on Google AI Pro and Ultra plans in the Antigravity app and CLI.
pricingNote: Free for individuals with rate limits; Google AI Pro and Ultra unlock more capacity. Google marks the free plan's Claude and GPT-OSS models for removal Nov 30, 2026.
strength: Google's agentic coding platform across an app, CLI, IDE, and SDK.
watchOut: The free individual plan has rate limits; Google AI Pro and Ultra unlock more capacity. The free plan's Claude and GPT-OSS models are marked for removal on Nov 30, 2026.

Microsoft 365 users who want AI in their apps

chat plus multi-step work across connected apps
research and everyday questions with a free start

It works in the Meta AI app, on meta.ai, in WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram, and Facebook, and with Meta's AI glasses.

quick image creation and photo edits
answers that draw on Instagram, Facebook, and Threads

name: Spacefast
rankReason: Gives what your AI builds a live link, hosting, and a database with no setup. Works with Next.js, Astro, TanStack Start, and PHP.
tagline: Automattic's publishing home for apps and sites your AI builds, with a live link in the chat
description: Spacefast is a new company from Automattic, the team behind WordPress.com, launched on November 9, 2026. It is not an AI builder itself: you keep working in Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, or another agent, and Spacefast gives that agent building instructions, a database, and hosting, then returns a live link right in the chat. Each project gets its own Space that is private by default, saves a version with every change so you can roll back, and supports comments pinned on the page that your AI can turn into fixes. Spaces also include file uploads and built-in visitor stats. You can publish without an account, or use the drop.fast drag-and-drop page, Git pushes, or the npx spacefast CLI. It supports Next.js, TanStack Start, Astro, and PHP projects, and Automattic says app authentication, transactional email, and shared team knowledge are coming in the next few weeks.
bestFor: publishing what ChatGPT or Claude builds without setting up hosting
sharing private drafts and collecting comments on the page
small apps that need a ready database

name: Devin Desktop (formerly Windsurf)
rankReason: An agentic IDE for managing several coding agents in one place, with a free plan.

description: Devin Desktop is the new name for Windsurf, Cognition's AI IDE. Apps sleep when nobody is using them and are billed by how long the machine is awake; they are rolling out gradually.
bestFor: managing several coding agents in one place

OpenCode 2.0, announced October 12, 2026, added a shared background server for all clients, background subagents, a Code Mode for tool calls, and an embeddable SDK.

strength: Open source AI coding agent for terminal, IDE, and desktop.

name: Cline
rankReason: A free, open-source coding agent for VS Code and other editors. Bring your own API keys and pay only for model use.
tagline: Open source coding agent for VS Code, JetBrains, Cursor, Windsurf, the CLI, and desktop
description: Cline is an open source AI coding agent that runs in VS Code, JetBrains, Cursor, and Windsurf, plus a CLI and a desktop app. It plans and makes multi-file changes, runs commands, and uses MCP tools, with your own API keys or the Cline provider. It also retries interrupted provider responses up to 3 times and fixes timeouts on long local-model requests.

strength: Open source coding agent for VS Code and the terminal; individual developers pay only for inference.

name: Zed
rankReason: A fast, open-source editor that runs outside agents like Claude Agent and Codex CLI. Free with your own API keys.
tagline: Fast open source code editor with a built-in AI agent
description: Zed is a fast, open source code editor with an Agent Panel, edit predictions, and support for external agents such as Claude Agent and Codex CLI through the Agent Client Protocol (ACP). Zed 1.27.0 (November 4, 2026) writes AI commit messages in the style of your three most recent commits, cuts Agent Panel memory and CPU use on long threads, and speeds up the Git Graph. It also removed agent checkpoints (reject edits or use Git to undo) and now requires macOS 12 Monterey or later. Zed ships weekly releases.
bestFor: running external coding agents in one editor

strength: Fast open source code editor with a built-in agent that can also run external agents.

name: Kiro
rankReason: AWS's spec-driven coding agent for larger codebases, with parallel agents and 50 free credits a month.
tagline: AWS's spec-driven agentic IDE, CLI, and web agent
description: Kiro is an agentic coding tool built and operated by AWS. It turns prompts into requirements, designs, and task lists (specs), then implements them with parallel agents, and checks behavior with property-based tests. It runs as an IDE that supports Open VSX extensions and VS Code settings, a CLI, and Kiro Web, and works with MCP, AGENTS.md, and the Agent Client Protocol. name: SciGround
tagline: Checks the statistics behind AI-assisted research outside the model, from design to claim
description: SciGround, launched by Licklider, Inc. of Tokyo on November 13, 2026, is a mathematical verification layer for research done with AI assistants. You keep using your own assistant, and it calls SciGround over MCP (SciGround MCP is in public beta, v0.1.0). The calculations run outside the model in established software such as SciPy, NumPy, R, FLINT/Arb, and the Z3 solver, with versions recorded. The test, direction, and threshold are fixed before results are shown, and if the design or data do not fit a supported workflow, SciGround refuses or pauses instead of approximating. It checks that the data match the design, that the numbers hold within a stated error bound, and that the claim follows from the result, and returns a machine-readable record others can rebuild. Launch workflows include t-tests, paired t-tests, one-way ANOVA, the Mann-Whitney U test, several outcomes with a correction, and bulk RNA-seq differential expression with FDR control.

name: llama.cpp
tagline: Free, open-source engine for running AI models locally on your own laptop, phone, or server
description: llama.cpp is the open-source C and C++ library and toolkit from the ggml-org team for running large language models and multimodal models on your own hardware, from consumer laptops to enterprise servers, using quantization and optimized backends. name: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol

You bring your own AI provider with an API key or your ChatGPT plan, or connect an open-source model running locally. It stops when your laptop sleeps, and each installation has one owner.

It includes transcription for 50+ languages with speaker diarization, context biasing, and end-of-turn detection, a realtime transcription model under 500 ms latency, and a text-to-speech model with emotion, pacing, and emphasis control across 35+ languages and 50+ dialects. A voice agent SDK built on LiveKit combines listening, reasoning, tool calling, and speaking in one streaming pipeline, over SIP or WebRTC. It runs on Mistral's EU, US, or global API or on your own infrastructure.
pricingNote: API from $0.0035 per minute for transcription; TTS $13 per 1M characters; voice agent API from $0.04 per minute
strength: Transcription, expressive speech, and a real-time voice agent SDK.
watchOut: This listing is API-priced only: transcription from $0.0035 a minute, TTS $13 per 1M characters, and voice agent from $0.04 a minute.

name: Deepgram
tagline: Speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and voice agent APIs for developers
description: Deepgram is a speech AI platform with APIs for transcription, text-to-speech, voice agents, and audio intelligence. On October 23, 2026 its Nova-3 Multilingual model expanded to 55 languages in a single model, for both pre-recorded and streaming audio, with code-switching when speakers change languages mid-conversation and a new language_hint parameter to bias detection toward the languages you expect. In October it also added Nova-3 Medical Multilingual for medical audio in 10 languages. Other options include Flux for real-time speech recognition in voice agents, speaker diarization, smart formatting, and keyterm prompting, plus Flux TTS and Aura-2 text-to-speech and a Voice Agent API. Billing is per second with no rounding up, there is a dedicated EU endpoint, and Enterprise customers can self-host or sign a HIPAA BAA.
pricingNote: $200 free credit with no card; pay as you go from $0.0043 per minute for Nova-3 pre-recorded and $0.0077 per minute streaming (Nova-3 Multilingual $0.0052 and $0.0092); diarization included on pre-recorded audio; Growth from $4,000 a year saves up to 20%; Enterprise is custom
strength: Speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and voice agent APIs for developers, with diarization included on pre-recorded audio.
watchOut: The $200 credit is a one-time free credit with no card, not a lasting free plan; Growth starts at $4,000 a year.

name: Cartesia
tagline: Fast text to speech, speech to text, and managed voice agents for developers
description: Cartesia makes the Sonic text to speech models, the Ink speech to text models, and Managed Agents for building phone and voice agents, all sold on one credit system. It speaks 44 languages, offers instant voice cloning on paid plans and professional voice cloning from the Startup plan, and can provision phone numbers for agents. It is built for developers shipping real-time apps such as customer support, scheduling, and lead qualification lines.
bestFor: low-latency text to speech in real-time apps
building phone agents for support and scheduling
cloning a brand speaker for an app
pricingNote: Free plan with 20K credits a month (about 27 minutes of Sonic text to speech) and $1 of prepaid agent usage; Pro $5 a month with 100K credits and a commercial use license; Startup $49 a month with 1.25M credits and pro voice cloning; Scale $299 a month with 8M credits; agent calls $0.03 a minute (previously $0.06), plus $0.014 a minute for Cartesia phone numbers; LLM usage on calls is billed separately; Enterprise is custom
strength: Cheap to start, with text to speech, speech to text, and voice agents on one credit plan from $5 a month.
watchOut: It is a developer platform, not a consumer app: you build with its API, the free plan has no commercial license, and LLM usage on agent calls is billed separately.

name: AssemblyAI-TTS-1
tagline: Low-latency text to speech built for voice agents
description: AssemblyAI-TTS-1 is AssemblyAI's text-to-speech model for voice agents, generally available since October 27, 2026. It streams audio in about 90 ms in production and has unlimited concurrency on pay-as-you-go with no annual contract. It ships with more than 4,000 voices, instant voice cloning once you confirm the speaker's permission, word timestamps, and a choice of US or EU processing. At launch it speaks English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, and Portuguese, and AssemblyAI provides reference agents for LiveKit and Pipecat.
pricingNote: $15 per 1M characters, pay as you go, with every voice, language, and voice cloning included; volume pricing for committed usage
strength: Low-latency text to speech built for voice agents, with every voice, language, and voice cloning included in the pay-as-you-go price.
watchOut: There is no free plan listed; volume pricing is for committed usage.

name: Phonic-1
tagline: Speech-to-speech voice agent model that acts while the caller talks
description: Phonic-1 is a speech-to-speech model from Phonic for voice agents, released October 29, 2026. It hears the caller's audio directly and answers in speech, with under 600 ms from speech in to speech out, and Phonic says it is the only speech-to-speech model that can call tools while the caller is still talking. It handles interruptions and turn-taking on noisy lines, speaks more than 50 languages with switching mid-conversation in the same voice, and pronounces URLs, emails, and codes accurately. You build on it with the API, TypeScript and Python SDKs, a CLI, or a no-code agent builder, and Phonic offers SOC 2 Type II, HIPAA with a BAA, and zero data retention.
bestFor: phone voice agents that call tools
pricingNote: One price per minute starting at $0.07, with no LLM pass-through or per-token charges
strength: Speech-to-speech voice agent model that acts while the caller talks, with one price per minute and no LLM pass-through charges.
watchOut: No free plan is listed; the starting price is $0.07 per minute.

name: Zapier
tagline: No-code automation across thousands of apps
description: Zapier connects apps with Zaps and AI features so non-developers can automate handoffs between SaaS tools.
pricingNote: Free plan with 100 tasks a month and two-step Zaps; Professional starts at $19.99 per month billed annually ($29.99 monthly); Team and Enterprise for organizations; 14-day Professional trial with no card
strength: No-code automation across thousands of apps, with a free plan for two-step Zaps.
watchOut: The free plan is limited to 100 tasks a month and two-step Zaps; listed Professional prices start at the annual rate.

name: IBM Granite Speech 5.0
tagline: Open speech models for accurate, fast transcription and translation
description: Granite Speech 5.0 is IBM's latest open speech collection, released October 21, 2026. The new granite-speech-5.0-2b model transcribes English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, and Japanese, translates to and from English, supports keyword lists of up to 2,000 terms, and ranks second among open-weight models on the Open ASR Leaderboard's average English word error rate. The updated 470M Turbo CTC model adds multilingual transcription with native punctuation and runs about 1.6 times faster than before, and the refreshed 4.1 2B Plus model improves speaker attribution and timestamps for meetings and calls. All are Apache 2.0.
pricingNote: Free open weights (Apache 2.0) on Hugging Face
strength: Open speech models for accurate, fast transcription and translation, with Apache 2.0 weights on Hugging Face.
watchOut: You run the open weights yourself; this listing does not include a hosted plan.

name: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe
tagline: Open-weight promptable model for transcription, translation, and speaker labels
description: Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is an open-weight speech model from NVIDIA, released October 28, 2026. It transcribes 40 languages, translates 31 languages to or from English, and attributes speakers in 13, labeling up to 8 speakers in recordings up to an hour long. Because it is promptable, it can also answer questions about audio and return word timestamps. NVIDIA reports it ranks first among open-weight models on the Hugging Face Open ASR Leaderboard for English at 5.33% word error rate. It is a Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts model with about 34B total and 4.3B active parameters that runs on one H100 80GB GPU, with FP8 and NVFP4 versions for local RTX and DGX Spark machines. It is built for recorded audio rather than live streaming.
bestFor: transcribing long recordings with speaker labels
pricingNote: Free open weights under the OpenMDW-1.1 license, which allows commercial use, on Hugging Face and ModelScope; hosted endpoints from Baseten, DeepInfra, and Simplismart are priced by those providers
strength: Open-weight promptable model for transcription, translation, and speaker labels, under a license that allows commercial use.
watchOut: Hosted endpoints from Baseten, DeepInfra, and Simplismart are priced by those providers, not in this listing.

name: Fish Audio Drama 3
tagline: Text-to-speech you direct in plain language
description: Drama 3 is Fish Audio's most emotive text-to-speech model, released publicly October 13, 2026. You direct each line in plain words, add sighs, laughs, and pauses exactly where you want them, and scope effects like a whisper to specific words. It speaks 83 languages, handles multi-speaker scenes, and is available on fish.audio, the Fish Audio mobile apps, the API, and as open weights on Hugging Face. Fish Audio has extended the API launch price of $10 per million UTF-8 bytes (80% off the $50 list price) through November 30, 2026.
pricingNote: API $50 per 1M UTF-8 bytes of input text (about 180,000 English words), with a launch price of $10 through November 30, 2026; creator plans on fish.audio from free (8,000 credits a month) to Plus at $15 a month ($11 billed yearly) and Pro at $100 a month ($75 billed yearly); open weights free for commercial use under US$500K annual revenue
strength: Text-to-speech you direct in plain language, including character dialogue and audiobook-style performances.
watchOut: The API launch price of $10 per 1M UTF-8 bytes ends November 30, 2026, then $50 list; open weights are free for commercial use only under US$500K annual revenue.

name: Gradium Phonon
tagline: Open-source text to speech that runs on your own device
description: Phonon is an open-source on-device text-to-speech model from Gradium, the voice AI company founded by the cofounders of the Kyutai research lab, released October 21, 2026. It comes in 31M and 40M parameter versions, small enough to ship inside a mobile app or load in a browser tab, and speaks English, French, German, Spanish, and Portuguese in one model. Speech is generated locally, so text and audio stay on the device. It includes ready-made voices, speed control, and integrations for Rust, Python, Swift, and the browser through WebAssembly.
bestFor: private text to speech inside apps
speech in the browser and on embedded hardware

You start with a prompt, an outline, or a file, and an AI agent builds the draft, then you refine it by chat or edit it by hand. It imports PowerPoint and PDF files, connects to 25+ tools such as Slack, Notion, and Dropbox, and exports to PowerPoint, PDF, PNG, and Google Slides.

turning a document or outline into a presentation

strength: Fast AI presentations and documents with PowerPoint import and export, and a free plan to try it.
watchOut: Free credits run out and do not refill, free decks carry Gamma branding, and content on personal plans may train Gamma AI features unless you opt out.

strength: AI writing assistant for clarity and tone, with a free plan that includes 100 AI prompts a month.

DeepL also sells Write and Voice as separate products; this listing is for the translator.

team glossaries and formal or informal tone

description: Google Translate is a free website and app for translating text, websites, and documents between many languages. Developers can use the Cloud Translation API, which Google prices at $20 per million characters.

strength: A free, widely available translator for text and documents, with a documented API price if you need it in an app.

description: QuillBot is a writing assistant used for paraphrasing, grammar checks, summaries, citations, and related writing tasks, with extensions for Chrome, Word, and desktop apps. It also adds AI chat and design tools in the same account. A free plan covers basic paraphrasing and summaries with word limits; Premium unlocks higher limits and extra modes. QuillBot says tens of millions of writers use it, including students and professionals.

strength: A well-known free writing assistant for paraphrase, grammar, and citations, especially for students.

strength: AI writing and Q&A inside Notion, including Notion Agent, AI Meeting Notes, and Enterprise Search on Business.

a starting plan for one user and one project

name: Mintlify Autopilot
tagline: Always-on agent that keeps your docs in sync with your code
description: Autopilot is Mintlify's always-on documentation agent, launched in beta October 20, 2026. It watches your repos and the systems around them, such as Slack, your project tracker, and support tickets, drafts doc updates when code merges or the same question keeps coming in, and opens a pull request for your team to review. Nothing publishes until someone merges, and it learns your team's tone and update habits from the PRs you review.

name: TK by Medium

description: TK is a private, agentic notebook for writing and thinking from Medium, launched on November 9, 2026. You can call its AI assistant without leaving the page by typing @TK mid-sentence, for example to check a fact or pull in a paragraph you wrote earlier. It ships with AI skills for editorial and headline feedback, can match a draft to the style guides of Medium publications, and turns any search, topic, tag, or library into a wiki-style summary page that links back to your notes. It imports your Medium archive plus vaults from Bear and Obsidian, imports and exports Markdown, and includes an MCP server and a Claude skill so your own agent can read what you have written. Medium says no AI company trains on your writing without your permission. Shared social libraries let you get human feedback on drafts.

turning scattered notes into organized ideas
giving your AI agent access to your own notes and drafts

name: KudoNovel
tagline: Browser app for writing novels with AI, now with an Autopilot mode that keeps the story going on its own
description: KudoNovel is a browser app for writing novels with its built-in AI, KudoAI. On November 18, 2026 it launched Autopilot: you press one button on an empty paragraph, it drafts where the story is heading (you can edit that direction or leave it to KudoAI), then writes three beats in a row in full prose, pausing so you can continue or take over. Every six beats it proposes a fresh direction to confirm. It writes with a story bible of characters, places, and events plus a running summary of the book, both kept up to date as you write. Everything it writes is ordinary editable text, and one step clears or undoes an Autopilot run. It works in modern browsers on computers and phones, in 22 languages.

pricingNote: Free sign-up with no card and one KudoAI credit after confirming your email; one-off credit packs from $3.50, no subscription
